source_note: Curated from statute-distill_lex-allium/bsa-aml-corpus/censuses (census_statutes_regs, census_fincen, census_fba_ffiec, census_sro_enforcement; census as_of 2026-07). Scope: ratified PS ps-aml-prog-001 v0.2 — AML/CFT program-establishment obligations, banks + MSBs + broker-dealers incl. FINRA SRO layer. Snapshot policy DL-002 (2026-07-18; pending = horizon). Completeness classes: statutes/regulations = census; guidance/manual/SRO = curated_set; enforcement = official_index_census (index-level).

items.title: Federal banking agency BSA-related formal actions
items.issuer: OCC / Federal Reserve / FDIC / NCUA (each self-publishes)
items.locator: OCC EASearch: https://apps.occ.gov/EASearch ; FRB: https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/enforcementactions.htm ; FDIC ED&O: https://orders.fdic.gov/s/ ; NCUA: https://ncua.gov/regulation-supervision/enforcement-actions
items.note: Index-level entry (OCC EASearch is filterable by 'Bank Secrecy Act/Money Laundering' category (hundreds of formal actions since 1990s; roughly 5-15 BSA-related formal actions/yr recently, e.g., Community Federal Savings Bank May 2026, a Northeast FSA April 2026). FRB: BSA-cited written agreements/C&Ds typically <10/yr. FDIC ED&O: monthly lists; BSA consent orders concentrated in community banks (e.g., Quaint Oak Bank, 2025-05-15). NCUA: fewest; mostly LUAs/administrative, occasional BSA orders.). CEILING: evidences applied expectations; never independently establishes an operative duty.

items.title: SEC / FINRA / CFTC AML enforcement
items.issuer: SEC (Administrative Proceedings + Litigation Releases, sec.gov); FINRA (Disciplinary Actions Online database + monthly disciplinary reports + AWC letters); CFTC (enforcement actions page)
items.note: Index-level entry (FINRA AML actions: 14 (2024) -> 20 (2025), ~$6.5-10M in AML fines 2025 (total FINRA sanctions 2025: $154M, +77% YoY); AML has been a FINRA exam/enforcement priority every year since 2002. SEC brings a handful of standalone 17a-8/SAR cases per year. CFTC standalone BSA cases remain rare (first: Interactive Brokers 2020).). CEILING: evidences applied expectations; never independently establishes an operative duty.
